title: Quarry Works inference intake jotter
content:
Call summary (Quarry Works / intake) — 2025-08-21
Attendees: Maya (RW SE), Ethan (RW SE), Priya (Solutions Eng), Tom B. (Quarry lead), Liza M. (Quarry infra), Rajesh (Quarry data/telemetry)

High-level customer context:
- Quarry Works is an industrial equipment monitoring platform (predictive maintenance + anomaly detection) serving ~1.2k active on-site gateways.
- Goal: add a short-form conversational interface + automated incident summarization that runs close to the edge/region. They want private deployment (VPC) and customer-managed key material.
- Must meet strict latency SLAs for interactive queries (target p95 < 250ms for single-turn status queries) and batch summarization offline.

Primary asks from call:
1) Private deployment (Redwood Private) behind their VPC — no customer data leaves VPC in production workflows.
2) Per-tenant audit logs and 90-day retention; exportable to their Splunk endpoint.
3) Ability to pin an internal model and have automated fallback to an open quantized variant if capacity limited.
4) Real-time telemetry ingestion: small prompt + last 128 token context from gateway; inexpensive per-interaction cost.
5) Role-based access controls for team members + HSM/KMS integration for model keys.

Notes / gotchas observed on call (raw):
- Their telemetry payloads are noisy: system logs interleaved with binary sensor blobs. Pre-tokenization step needed to extract textual context reliably (Liza).
- They insisted on determinism for certain templates (incident summary templates). We should document variance expectations for generative outputs and recommend structured output / function call mode for required fields.
- They will do on-prem gateway inference in some countries — need to confirm regulatory boundary for private control plane vs on-prem runtime.
- Tokenization surprises: some embedded telemetry labels use non-UTF8 char sequences; tokenizer crashed once during demo (Tom). Need prevalidate and replace nonprintables.
- They asked for redaction hooks before storage: PII, device serial numbers, technician names — add pre-store transform.

Technical constraints and initial proposals:
- Model selection: recommend a smaller instruction-tuned 13B (quantized to 4/8-bit) for interactive queries to meet latency and cost. For long-form summarization use a 70B offline variant in Dedicated mode for nightly jobs.
- Serving suggestion: Dedicated capacity in-region with a small private pool (2x A100-80GB equiv) as a starting commit. Reserve 40% headroom for bursting. Rationale: target p95 <250ms for single-turn with 13B quantized.
- Batching policy: recommend micro-batching (0.5–1s window) for async summarization routes; for interactive routes enforce immediate throughput (no batching) or tiny batch=2 with strict latency SLO.
- Caching: prefix cache at gateway-level (store last 256 tokens per device) + server-side KV cache for common templates and static context (firmware versions, device metadata).
- KV cache eviction: LRU with TTL ~6h for telemetry keys, TTL ~30d for firmware metadata.
- Security: KMS/HSM for model keys + customer-managed CMEK for storage. Audit logs pushed to their Splunk using syslog sink; Redwood Console will maintain an index for ops.
- Observability: add tracing hooks (X-Request-ID from gateway) and per-token latency breakdown. Need to ensure token-level traces are scrubbed of PII.

Prompt engineering / reliability notes:
- Use function-calling for incident summaries to guarantee fields (title, severity, top-3 actions, confidence). This reduces hallucination and eases downstream automation.
- For interactive status queries: short instruction prompt + 3-turn system memory. Keep prompts under 250 tokens to preserve latency.
- Example assistant instruction (rough):
  "You are an assistant for Quarry Works. Given latest telemetry and device metadata, return a status: one of [OK, WARNING, CRITICAL], a short rationale (<=40 words), and list up to 2 remediation steps. Output as JSON via function call."
- Quality checks: add a lightweight eval harness (50 golden prompts) in Redwood Console to monitor regression when we change quantization/kernel. Hook alerts to Slack #qw-ops.

Cost and perf roughbacks-of-envelope (initial):
- Interactive 13B quantized: estimated 0.4–0.7 tokens/sec effective decode speed per A100-v2 stream; expect 60–120ms per 32-token response (rough). Unit cost estimate to be refined after perf runs.
- Nightly summarization (70B): batch jobs ~6–8 hours with Dedicated pool; schedule off-peak to reduce cost.

Rollout / canary plan (initial idea):
- Phase 0: Proof-of-concept with 1 region, non-prod private deployment (sandbox VPC). Run 2 weeks with a small subset of gateways (50 devices) to validate tokenization, redaction, latency.
- Phase 1: Private deployment (prod) with pinned 13B model, Dedicated pool (2 GPUs). Canary 5% traffic for 24h, expand to 25% over 48h if no major errors.
- Phase 2: Enable nightly summarization on Dedicated 70B. Run for 7 days, compare outputs to legacy pipeline.

Action items (owners + dates):
- Maya: deliver perf probing script + sample prompts to QW by 2025-08-26.
- Ethan: prototype pre-tokenization sanitizer (strip nonprintables + label extraction) and share Docker image by 2025-09-01.
- Priya: draft compliance checklist (KMS/HSM integration + audit pipeline) and Confluence page link by 2025-08-29.
- Liza (Quarry): provide example telemetry payloads (raw, redacted) and Splunk ingestion endpoint by 2025-08-28.
- Rajesh (Quarry): nominate 50 pilot gateways and a contact for on-site testing by 2025-09-04.

Open questions to resolve in follow-up:
- Does their legal team require on-prem control plane (we proposed private control plane with customer-managed network) — follow up 1:1 with legal.
- Exact Splunk ingestion schema for audit logs and mapping for token-level traces (we need field names).
- Which countries require on-prem runtime vs VPC-only private deployment (regulatory).
- Expected concurrency (QPS) during 3 peak windows — Tom to share heatmap for us to size Dedicated pool further.

Random notes / to-self:
- Remember to recommend preflight tokenizer run for all historical device logs before import (avoid sporadic crashes).
- Consider shipping small wasm-based sanitizer at gateway for nonprintable stripping to reduce payload drops.
- When we run perf tests, capture kernel selection logs (help with quantization tuning).

Next meeting: propose 2025-09-03 10:00 PT (internal sync 09:00 PT). Suggest include product + security for KMS/retention discussion.

End of jotter — will iterate as artifacts come in.
